quote: Naturally, one may wonder whether the following statement is actually also true: For 0 < β ≤ 1, (α_1, . . . , α_n) ⪯^p (α*_1, . . . , α*_n) gives rise to the usual stochastic order between X_{1:n} and X*_{1:n}. The following example gives negative answer to these two conjecture. Example 3. Let (X_1, X_2) ((X*_1, X*_2)) be a vector of independent heterogeneous GMW random variables. Set β = 0.5, γ = 2 and λ = 3. For (α_1, α_2) = (2, 3) ⪯^p (1, 5.5) = (α*_1, α*_2), X_{1:2} ≥_st X*_{1:2}, as can be seen in Fig. 3 (A); however, for (α_1, α_2) = (1.1, 6) ⪯^p (1, 2.25) = (α*_1, α*_2), X_{1:2} ≤_st X*_{1:2}, as can be seen in Fig. 3 (B) So, (α_1, α_2) ⪯^p (α*_1, α*_2) implies neither X_{1:2} ≤_st X*_{1:2} nor X_{1:2} ≥_st X*_{1:2} for 0 < β ≤ 1.
